name: Environment Agency: Water situation reports, Thames area (monthly)
gives: end-of-month storage percent for Farmoor and the Lower Thames Reservoirs, with comparison to the long-term average
national reservoir stocks for England; rainfall, river flow and groundwater context

why.quote: All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated
why.basis: publication page (Last updated 17 November 2026), as quoted by a page reader; Crown copyright. Summary pages state 'All data are provisional and may be subject to revision.' robots.txt (https://www.gov.uk/robots.txt, 200): 'User-agent: * / Disallow: /*/print$ / Disallow: /search/all*'.

interface: HTML summary page per area per month plus a PDF full report (Thames Area October 2026: 28 pages, 3.16 MB). Summary: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/water-situation-local-area-reports/thames-water-situation-october-2026-summary . PDF: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6afb08769be17c68c69ca8f6/Thames_Area_water_situation_report_October_2026.pdf . No key. A national equivalent: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/water-situation-national-monthly-reports-for-england-2026 (October 2026 added 11 Nov 2026).
notes: Read 18 Nov 2026: the collection, area and national publication pages, and the Thames October summary (HTML), not the PDFs. Summary says (end of October 2026): Farmoor 74% of capacity, up from 69%, 15% below the long-term average; Lower Thames Reservoirs 51.9%, down from 53.1% (matches the London Datastore 53 for 30 Sep), 24% lower than average. Updated mid-month for the previous month, so about 2 to 3 weeks behind: fresher than the Datastore CSV. Free text in HTML, so extraction needs care. Page URLs follow a pattern per month but the asset PDF links carry hashes.
